provinces.name: Ontario
provinces.analysis:
Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey recorded Ontario unemployment at 7.5%5, with the participation rate at 64.8% and the employment rate at 59.9%5. Provincial GDP registered +1.2% and CPI +2.9%1, while CMHC reported housing starts at 62,735 units5.

Ontario's 2026 Budget tabled a 10-year capital plan exceeding $210B ($37B in 2026-27); the pipeline tracks 729 projects worth roughly $360.0B, with infrastructure the largest sector (198 projects, $123.1B). Unemployment is 7.5% (highest among the large provinces) while April 2026 LFS showed Ontario employment rose +0.5%, the only large-province gain; the database tracks 729 projects across 18 sectors.1

The Ontario Line ($27.43B, Under Construction) and GO Expansion ($26.08B, Under Construction) anchor a Transit & Rail bloc; the budget adds $11.0B to transit over 2025-26 to 2027-28. CPI is +2.9% and GDP +1.2%; 245 of 729 tracked projects are Under Construction and 193 Proposed.1

Ontario's pipeline tracks 729 projects worth roughly $360.0B across 18 sectors. The largest blocs are infrastructure (198 projects, $123.1B), mining (25 projects, $80.1B) and power_energy (15 projects, $66.3B). Manufacturing exposure (13 projects, $60.6B) routes CAD/USD and steel/copper price moves into auto-parts and equipment capital plans; the Ontario Line ($27.43B) and GO Expansion ($26.08B) anchor rate-sensitive transit financing.1

provinces.name: Quebec
provinces.analysis:
Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey recorded Quebec unemployment at 6.2%5, with the participation rate at 64.4% and the employment rate at 60.4%5. Provincial GDP registered +1.3% and CPI -0.4%1, while CMHC reported housing starts at 53,461 units5.

Hydro-Quebec is advancing a ~$145-185B decade-long capacity plan; the pipeline tracks 520 Quebec projects worth ~$78.4B, led by power_energy (29 projects, $35.4B). Quebec posted the largest provincial employment decline in April 2026 (-43,000; -0.9%) per StatCan LFS while carrying the lowest large-province unemployment (6.2%); 520 projects are tracked across the province.1

Quebec is the only province with negative CPI (-0.4%); the pipeline includes the $9.00B Parc eolien zone Chamouchouane (Proposed) and the $4.89B Montreal Metro Blue Line Extension (Under Construction). 292 of 520 tracked Quebec projects are Approved and 37 Under Construction; education (118 projects) and infrastructure (103) are the largest sectors by count.1

Quebec's pipeline tracks 520 projects worth ~$78.4B. The largest sectors by value are power_energy (29 projects, $35.4B), mining (24 projects, $19.9B) and infrastructure (103 projects, $18.1B). Hydro-Quebec's ~$145-185B capacity plan drives the power_energy bloc; the $9.00B Parc eolien zone Chamouchouane and $4.89B Montreal Metro Blue Line Extension are the largest single entries, exposing the pipeline to electricity-build financing and rate conditions.1

provinces.name: Alberta
provinces.analysis:
Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey recorded Alberta unemployment at 7.0%4, with the participation rate at 69.2% and the employment rate at 64.4%4. Provincial GDP registered +2.7% and CPI +1.3%1, while CMHC reported housing starts at 46,064 units4.

The Pathways Alliance CCS complex (~$16.5B in the database) was cleared for construction under the federal-Alberta energy 'grand bargain'; the pipeline tracks 734 Alberta projects worth ~$346.9B, led by power_energy (125 projects, $137.3B). Alberta carries the highest participation rate nationally (69.2%) with unemployment at 7.0%; 408 of 734 tracked projects are Proposed.1

Alberta is targeting $100B in data-centre investment with proposals now requesting >20 GW of power; the $50.00B Olds AI Data Centre Hub (Proposed) is the single largest tracked project. CPI is +1.3% (among the lowest provincial readings) and GDP +2.7%; the federal-provincial carbon-credit price was set at $130/tonne.1

Alberta's pipeline tracks 734 projects worth ~$346.9B. The largest sectors are power_energy (125 projects, $137.3B), manufacturing (34 projects, $65.8B) and oil_gas (26 projects, $44.4B). WTI, WCS and natural-gas prices flow through to the oil_gas and CCS capital plans, while the $50.00B Olds AI Data Centre Hub and Wonder Valley data-centre park tie the pipeline to power-price and electricity-supply conditions amid >20 GW of requested data-centre load.1

provinces.analysis:

BC carries the largest provincial pipeline at ~$511.3B across 694 projects. The largest sectors are power_energy (68 projects, $202.7B), mining (57 projects, $70.0B) and oil_gas (13 projects, $53.2B). Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey recorded Nunavut unemployment at 12.0%4, with the participation rate at 62.5% and the employment rate at 55.0%4. Provincial GDP registered +7.5% and CPI N/A1. CPI and housing-starts series are not published on a sub-annual cadence for this territory; the LFS reading carries the labour signal.

The Grays Bay Road and Port Project (~$1.2B) filed an impact statement with the Nunavut Impact Review Board on March 1, 2026; the proponent says it could lift Nunavut GDP ~20%. The pipeline tracks 47 NU projects (smallest count of any region) worth ~$2.0B. Nunavut carries the highest unemployment (12.0%) and lowest employment rate (55.0%) of all 16 regions, with the strongest regional GDP reading at +7.5% (2024 annual cadence).1

B2Gold's Goose mine entered production targeting 300,000 oz gold in 2026; the Back River Gold Project ($0.61B, Under Construction) is the largest tracked entry. 30 of 47 tracked NU projects are Under Construction; infrastructure (13 projects, $0.6B) is the largest sector by count.1

Nunavut's pipeline tracks 47 projects (the smallest count of any region) worth ~$2.0B. The largest sectors are mining (1 project, $0.6B), infrastructure (13 projects, $0.6B) and environment (5 projects, $0.2B). The Back River Gold Project ($0.61B, Under Construction) ties the pipeline to gold pricing as B2Gold's Goose mine ramps to 300,000 oz in 2026; the ~$1.2B Grays Bay road/port is the key infrastructure catalyst pending NIRB review.1
